title: Fondue Volcano Island
seo_title: Fondue Volcano Charcuterie Board: Gruyère Lava & What to Buy
description: A fondue volcano board for 12 to 15: a sourdough volcano erupting Gruyère and Emmental fondue, with seared kielbasa, chorizo and an island of dippers.
hook: A sourdough volcano erupting molten Swiss fondue, with lava running down its sides onto an island of dippers.

items.name: Soft pretzel rolls or a bag of pretzel bites

why: The volcano is a hollowed loaf of sourdough, and the lava refills itself: hot Gruyère and Emmental fondue is poured in and spills over the edges. Guests dip seared kielbasa, chorizo, bread and vegetables straight into it.
The warm fondue makes it a perfect winter party board. Keep a pot of fondue warm on the stove and top up the volcano as it goes down.

timeline.what: Shred the cheeses and toss them with cornstarch. Cut the bread cubes and let them dry slightly, uncovered. Cut and store the dippers.
Roast the potatoes and char the broccolini. Sear the sausages.
Carve the boule and arrange all the dippers around it.
Make the fondue, pour it into the crater, and keep the rest warm in a fondue pot.

faq.q: What cheese is best for fondue?
faq.a: Gruyère and Emmental, the classic Swiss pair. Gruyère brings flavor and Emmental makes it smooth and stretchy.

faq.q: Can I make it without wine?
faq.a: Yes. The book gives a version made with low-sodium chicken broth and a little lemon juice.

faq.q: How do you keep the fondue warm?
faq.a: Keep the main pot on low heat or in a fondue pot and refill the bread volcano every 15 to 20 minutes.
